# New renderings — iliad-085 (13.748–837)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (13.750; departure from 1.201 in the pronoun and from 2.7 and 4.312 in the `i` naming; μιν is Polydamas, Hector is the speaker) | "and, lifting his voice, to him winged words he spoke:" | "and lifting his voice he spoke winged words to Polydamas:" | "to her" (the published English of 1.201, where μιν is Athena), "to him" in `i` (the unit has two men in it and Hector is the subject of the sentence, so a bare "him" would be read as Hector; the Dream is named in the same way at 2.7) |
| αὐτοῦ ἐρύκακε πάντας ἀρίστους (13.751; αὐτοῦ "on the spot", set against κεῖσε "there") | "on the spot hold back all the best" | "hold all the best men back here" | "stay here yourself" (loses the order to hold the chiefs), "keep back" ; ἐρύκω keeps "hold back" (ἠρύκακε 5.321 "held back") |
| ἐπὴν εὖ τοῖς ἐπιτείλω (13.753; same half-line as 10.62, iliad-058) | "when I have given them good charge" | "once I have charged them properly" (+ "I shall quickly come back" around it) | reused from the published line; αἶψα keeps "quickly" |
| ὄρεϊ νιφόεντι ἐοικώς (13.754) | "to a snowy mountain likened" | "like a snowy mountain" (+ note: the Greek gives no point of likeness) | "gleaming like a snow-capped mountain", "towering" (each decides the point of comparison); ἐοικώς "like", νιφόεις "snowy" |
| Πανθοΐδης (Πουλυδάμας, 13.756) | "Panthous’-son" | "son of Panthous" | "Panthoides", "Panthoïd"; follows Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" / "son of Atreus" |
| ἀγαπήνορα Πουλυδάμαντα (13.756; ἀγαπήνωρ, sense not known) | "the man-cherishing Polydamas" | "Polydamas … who prized manliness" (+ note: exact sense unknown) | "the manly", "high-hearted", "beloved"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀγαπήνορα Λαοδάμαντα (7.170 row) |
| βίη Ἑλένοιο ἄνακτος (13.758, 770, 781) | "the might of lord Helenus" | "the might of lord Helenus" | "mighty Helenus", "Helenus, the strong" (each drops the periphrasis); ἄναξ "lord" |
| Ἀσιάδης (Ἀδάμας, 13.759, 771) | "Asius’-son Adamas" | "Adamas son of Asius" | "Adamas the Asiad", "Asiades"; patronymics as for Ἀτρεΐδης |
| φοίτα ἀνὰ προμάχους (13.760) | "went to and fro among the front-fighters" | "went to and fro among the foremost fighters" | "ranged through the champions", "ran"; φοιτάω "go to and fro" (5.528, 9.9), πρόμαχοι "front-fighters" / "foremost fighters" (4.495) |
| εἴ που ἐφεύροι (13.760, no object) | "in case anywhere he might find them" | "in case he might find them anywhere" | follows 5.168 (iliad-028), "in case anywhere he might find him", with the plural pronoun |
| ἀνολέθρους (13.761) | "undestroyed" | "free from destruction" | "unscathed" (the same as ἀπήμων "unharmed"), "unruined", "unperished"; ὄλεθρος "destruction" (αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος "steep destruction") |
| οὐκέτι πάμπαν (13.761; negative context) | "no longer at all" | "no longer at all" | "no longer altogether", "no longer wholly" (the table’s πάμπαν "altogether" is for positive contexts, "not at all" for negative ones, 13.348) |
| ψυχὰς ὀλέσαντες (13.763) | "having lost their souls" | "having lost their lives" | "souls" in `i` (the table’s ψυχή "soul" keeps `l`; the English idiom for death is "lost their lives"), "perishing", "dying" |
| νηυσὶν ἔπι πρυμνῇσιν (13.762) | "at the sterns of the ships" | "at the sterns of the ships" | "the hindmost ships", "the sternmost ships"; follows ἐπὶ πρυμνῇσι νέεσσιν (13.333) |
| ἐν τείχει (13.764; the Greek does not say whose wall) | "within the wall" | "within the wall" (+ note: probably Troy’s, not said) | "inside Troy’s wall", "behind the wall" (each decides which wall) |
| τὸν δὲ τάχ’ εὗρε (13.765) | "And him soon he found" | "Soon he found him" | "quickly" (kept for αἶψα), "perhaps"; follows the table’s τάχα "soon" (13.676) |
| μάχης ἐπ’ ἀριστερὰ δακρυοέσσης (13.765) | "on the left of tearful battle" | "on the left of the tearful battle" | "grievous", "weeping"; follows ἐπ’ ἀριστερὰ μάχης "on the left of the battle" (5.355) and δακρυόεις "tearful" |
| θαρσύνονθ’ ἑτάρους καὶ ἐποτρύνοντα μάχεσθαι (13.767) | "cheering his companions and urging them on to fight" | "cheering his companions and urging them on to fight" | "comrades" (ἑταῖρος keeps "companions", as in iliad-058, iliad-082); ἐποτρύνω "urge on" (13.94) |
| ἀγχοῦ δ’ ἱστάμενος προσέφη αἰσχροῖς ἐπέεσσι (13.768) | "and standing near he addressed him with shameful words" | "and standing close by he spoke to him with shameful words" | "reviled" (kept for νείκεσσεν, 3.38), "abusive"; προσέφη "addressed" (l) / "spoke to" (i); αἰσχροῖς ἐπέεσσι "shameful words" as at 3.38 |
| ποῦ τοι + names (13.770, 772) | "where for you are Deiphobus …" · "And where for you is Othryoneus?" | "where are Deiphobus …" · "And where is Othryoneus?" | "where are your …" (a "your" before a name reads as ownership; the dative τοι is "to you, for you"), "tell me, where" |
| κατ’ ἄκρης (13.772, of Ilios) | "from the top down" | "from the top down" | "utterly" (loses ἄκρη "summit"), "to its foundations", "from its summit" ; the Odyssey ships "from on high" for a wave (25.313), where the sense is different |
| Ἴλιος αἰπεινή (13.773) | "Ilios, steep" | "steep Ilios" | "lofty", "towering", "sheer" ; αἰπεινός "steep" (Pedasus, 6.34) |
| νῦν τοι σῶς αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος (13.773) | "now for you sure is steep destruction" | "Now steep destruction is certain for you" | reused from the Odyssey (odyssey-106, Odyssey 22.28), with the closing quotation mark added; "safe" for σῶς (the usual sense, which would turn the line upside down) |
| ἐρωῆσαι πολέμοιο (13.776) | "to hold back from war" | "hold back from war" | "draw back from", "rest from", "withdraw" ; ἐρωέω "draw back" is the LSJ sense and "hold back" is kept for ἐρύκω in the same part, so the note tells the two apart |
| μέλλω ἐρωῆσαι (13.776–777) | "I am set to hold back" | "there may be some other time when I hold back" | "I am about to" (loses the sense that this is for another day), "I intend to"; follows the Odyssey’s μέλλεν … ἔμμεναι "was set to be" (odyssey-003) |
| οὐδ’ ἐμὲ πάμπαν ἀνάλκιδα γείνατο μήτηρ (13.777) | "not even me at all without might did my mother bear" | "my mother did not bear even me without might at all" | "a weakling", "cowardly" (kept for ἀνάλκις where the Odyssey ships it as a reproach), "unwarlike"; ἀνάλκις "without might" |
| μάχην ἤγειρας ἑταίρων (13.778) | "you roused the battle of companions" | "you stirred up the battle of our companions" | "the war", "the fighting of your comrades"; ἐγείρω "rouse"; "our" supplied in `i` because ἑταίρων is Trojan companions |
| ὁμιλέομεν Δαναοῖσι νωλεμέως (13.779–780) | "we are mingling with the Danaans unceasingly" | "we have been here mingling with the Danaans without pause" | "consorting", "fighting"; follows 11.523 (iliad-068) and νωλεμέως "unceasingly" / "without pause" |
| οἴω … οἴχεσθον (13.781–782; οἴω is the dual of οἶος, not ὀΐω "I think") | "The two alone … have gone" | "Only … have gone off" | "I think … have gone" (reads οἴω as ὀΐω), "are gone" alone; the note says οἴω is dual |
| μακρῇσι τετυμμένω ἐγχείῃσιν … κατὰ χεῖρα (13.782–783) | "struck with long spears … in the hand" | "struck in the hand by long spears" | "wounded", "pierced" (reserved for οὐτάω "wounded"), "through the hand"; τύπτω "strike" |
| φόνον δ’ ἤμυνε Κρονίων (13.783) | "but slaughter the son of Cronus warded off" | "but the son of Cronus warded off their slaughter" | "death", "murder", "kept death from them"; φόνος "slaughter" (the table’s φονή "slaughter"), ἀμύνω "ward off", Κρονίων "the son of Cronus" |
| πὰρ δύναμιν δ’ οὐκ ἔστι καὶ ἐσσύμενον πολεμίζειν (13.787) | "and beyond ability it is not possible, even for one eager, to fight" | "but beyond one’s ability there is no fighting, however eager one is" | "beyond one’s strength", "no man can fight beyond his power"; δύναμις "ability" as in the Odyssey’s ὅση δύναμίς γε πάρεστιν |
| ὣς εἰπὼν παρέπεισεν ἀδελφειοῦ φρένας ἥρως (13.788; the line of 7.120, where the speaker is Agamemnon, here Alexander) | "So having spoken, he talked round his brother’s wits, the hero;" | "So he spoke, and the hero talked his brother’s mind round;" | the published `l` and the first words of the published `i` kept; the rest of 7.120’s `i` ("with what was fitting, and Menelaus obeyed") belongs to another sentence and is not carried over |
| βὰν δ’ ἴμεν ἔνθα μάλιστα μάχη καὶ φύλοπις ἦεν (13.789) | "And they set out to go where most of all battle and battle-din was" | "And they set out to go where the battle and the din of battle were fiercest" | "where the fighting was thickest", "grimmest" ; βῆ δ’ ἴμεν "set out to go" (5.166), φύλοπις "battle-din" / "din of battle" |
| Names in 13.789–792 | Cebriones, Polydamas, Phalces, Orthaeus, Polyphetes, Palmys, Ascanius, Morys, Hippotion | same | "Phalkes", "Orthaios", "Polyphoetes", "Palmus", "Ascanios", "Moris"; the familiar Latinised forms, as for the other names |
| υἷ’ Ἱπποτίωνος (13.792; υἷ’ elided, usually the dual υἷε) | "the two sons of Hippotion" | "the sons of Hippotion" (+ note: dual or singular) | "Hippotion’s son" (takes the singular reading), "the sons" in `l` (loses the dual); follows the table’s Ἀτρεΐδα … "the two sons of Atreus" |
| ἀμοιβοί (13.793; "in exchange", of troops relieving others) | "as replacements" | "as replacements" | "as their relief", "in turn", "to take over"; the note explains the sense |
| ἠοῖ τῇ προτέρῃ (13.794) | "at the earlier dawn" | "the dawn before" | "yesterday", "the morning before", "at first light"; ἠώς "dawn" |
| ὑπὸ βροντῆς πατρὸς Διὸς εἶσι πέδον δέ (13.796) | "beneath the thunder of father Zeus goes to the ground" | "sweeps down to the earth beneath the thunder of father Zeus" | "to the plain", "falls to the ground" (πέδον is the ground; "plain" is kept for πεδίον); ἄελλα "blast" (`l`) / "storm" (`i`) as shipped |
| θεσπεσίῳ ὁμάδῳ (13.797) | "with wondrous uproar" | "with a wondrous uproar" | "din" (kept for ἠχή), "roar" (φλοῖσβος), "tumult"; θεσπέσιος "wondrous"; ὁμαδός "uproar" from the shipped ὁμάδησαν "made an uproar" |
| παφλάζοντα (13.798, of waves) | "seething" | "seething" | "bubbling", "boiling", "foaming", "roaring" (πολυφλοίσβοιο is "roaring") |
| κυρτά (13.799, of waves) | "arched" | "arched" | "curved", "humped", "swelling" |
| φαληριόωντα (13.799, of waves) | "white-flecked" | "white-flecked" | "white-capped", "foam-crested", "white-crested" (φάλος is a crest, which is not said), "whitening"; φαληριάω built on φαληρός "white-spotted" |
| πρὸ μέν τ’ ἄλλ’, αὐτὰρ ἐπ’ ἄλλα · πρὸ μὲν ἄλλοι … ἐπ’ ἄλλοι (13.799–800) | "some in front, but others upon others" · "some in front … but others after" | "some in front and others after them" · "some ranged in front and others behind" | "one after another", "wave on wave" (not in the Greek); the same pattern in both clauses, so the English keeps one pattern |
| ἀρηρότες (13.800) | "fitted close" | "ranged" | "firmly set", "in close order", "in serried ranks"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀρηρότες "fitted" (8.340) and `i` "ranged in a row" |
| χαλκῷ μαρμαίροντες (13.801) | "gleaming with bronze" | "gleaming with bronze" | "flashing", "glittering", "shining" (kept for φαεινός); μαρμαίρω "gleam" |
| ῥινοῖσιν πυκινήν (13.804, of a shield) | "solid with hides" | "solid with hides" | "close-packed", "thick", "dense"; πυκινός keeps "solid" (5.751); the note says the hides are layered |
| πολλὸς δ’ ἐπελήλατο χαλκός (13.804) | "much bronze had been driven on" | "much bronze had been hammered on" | "laid on", "beaten out", "overlaid"; ἐλαύνω "drive" as shipped (ἐλήλατο, 4.135 and 13.594) with ἐπί "on"; `i` "hammered" because the Greek verb is used of beaten metal |
| κροτάφοισι (13.805) | "temples" | "temples" | "brows", "sides of his head" |
| ἐπειρᾶτο (13.806) | "he made trial" | "he tried" | "he tested" ("tested" is kept for ἐπιπειράω of a bow), "he probed"; πειράω "try, make trial" |
| εἴ πώς οἱ εἴξειαν (13.807) | "if in some way they would yield to him" | "to see whether they would somehow give way to him" | "retreat", "break"; εἴκω "yield" |
| οὐ σύγχει θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν (13.808) | "he did not confound the heart in the breasts" | "he did not throw the heart in the Achaeans’ breasts into confusion" | "unnerve", "shake the courage", "disturb the spirit" (θυμός is "heart", not "courage"); συγχέω "confound" |
| Αἴας δὲ πρῶτος προκαλέσσατο (13.809) | "But Ajax first challenged him" | "But Ajax was the first to challenge him" | "Ajax spoke first" ; προκαλέσσατο "challenged" as at 7.217 and 7.285 |
| τί ἢ δειδίσσεαι αὔτως (13.810) | "why then do you frighten, just so" | "why try to frighten … to no purpose" | "for nothing" , "idly", "without cause" ("even without cause", the table’s sense at 1.520); αὔτως "just so" (`l`) / "to no purpose" (`i`, as at 2.342) |
| οὔ τοί τι μάχης ἀδαήμονές εἰμεν (13.811) | "We are not at all unacquainted with battle" | "We are not strangers to battle" | "ignorant of", "unskilled in"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀδαήμων "unacquainted" / "a stranger to" (17.283) |
| Διὸς μάστιγι κακῇ ἐδάμημεν (13.812) | "by the evil whip of Zeus we were overcome" | "we Achaeans were overcome by the evil whip of Zeus" | "cruel", "grievous" (kept for ἀργαλέος), "scourge"; follows Διὸς μάστιγι δαμέντες "overcome by the whip of Zeus" (12.37), κακός "evil" |
| ἦ θήν πού τοι θυμὸς ἐέλπεται (13.813) | "Truly, I suppose, your heart hopes" | "No doubt your heart hopes" | "surely", "I am sure" (kept for οὔ θήν, 2.276); ἔλπομαι "hope" (iliad-059, 10.103) |
| ἄφαρ δέ τε χεῖρες ἀμύνειν εἰσὶ καὶ ἡμῖν (13.814) | "and at once hands to defend are ours also" | "but we too have hands that are quick to defend" | "ready to repel", "fast"; ἄφαρ "at once" (iliad-004, iliad-006, iliad-011); ἀμύνειν εἰσί "are there to defend" (13.312) |
| ἦ κε πολὺ φθαίη εὖ ναιομένη πόλις ὑμὴ (13.815) | "Truly your well-inhabited city would be first by far" | "Surely your well-peopled city will be taken and sacked beneath our hands far sooner" | "would fall first", "would be sacked before"; φθάνω "be first" (10.368), εὖ ναιομένη "well-inhabited" (`l`) / "well-peopled" (`i`) as in the Odyssey’s Σιδονίην εὖ ναιομένην |
| ἁλοῦσά τε περθομένη τε (13.816) | "taken and being sacked" | "taken and sacked beneath our hands" | reused from 2.374 (iliad-011) |
| σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ φημὶ σχεδὸν ἔμμεναι ὁππότε (13.817) | "And for you yourself I say it is near, when" | "I say that the time is near when" | "I tell you that the day is near" (supplies "day"); the note says there is no stated subject |
| θάσσονας ἰρήκων ἔμεναι καλλίτριχας ἵππους (13.819) | "swifter than hawks to be, the fair-maned horses" | "that your fair-maned horses may be swifter than hawks" | "falcons" (κίρκος is "falcon", Odyssey 13.87), "faster than"; θάσσων "swifter" (ταχύς "swift"), ἴρηξ "hawk", καλλίτριχας "fair-maned" (5.321) |
| οἵ σε πόλιν δ’ οἴσουσι κονίοντες πεδίοιο (13.820) | "which will carry you to the city, raising dust over the plain" | "to carry you to the city as they raise dust over the plain" | "stirring the dust", "across the plain"; κονίω "raise dust", φέρω "carry" |
| θάρσυνος οἰωνῷ (13.823; rare, formed on θάρσος) | "emboldened by the bird of omen" | "emboldened by the bird of omen" | "encouraged", "heartened by the omen" ("omen" alone is avoided for οἰωνός, 15.532), "bold" (the adjective sense) |
| ἁμαρτοεπές (13.824; ἁμαρτάνω + ἔπος) | "errant in speech" | "you who speak wide of the mark" | "blunderer in words", "reckless-of-speech" (kept for ἀπτοεπής, 8.209), "babbler", "mis-speaking"; ἁμαρτάνω "miss" |
| ποῖον ἔειπες (13.824, no noun) | "what sort of thing you have said" | "what a thing you have said!" | "what sort of word" (ὁ μῦθος is not in the line); follows ποῖον τὸν μῦθον ἔειπες "what sort of word is this you have spoken" |
| εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼν οὕτω γε Διὸς πάϊς αἰγιόχοιο εἴην (13.825–826) | "if only I, so surely, were the son of aegis-bearing Zeus for all my days" | "If only I were the son of aegis-bearing Zeus for all my days" | "child of Zeus", "if only I were … as surely as" in `l` (the table’s εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼν ὣς "if only I, so surely"), "forever"; πάϊς "son" (Κρόνου πάϊς, 2.205; "the son of Ancaeus", 2.609) |
| τέκοι δέ με πότνια Ἥρη (13.826) | "and lady Hera had borne me" | "and lady Hera had borne me" | "and Hera were my mother", "lady Hera" kept; πότνια "lady", τίκτω "bear" |
| τιοίμην δ’ ὡς τίετ’ Ἀθηναίη καὶ Ἀπόλλων · ὡς νῦν ἡμέρη ἥδε κακὸν φέρει Ἀργείοισι (13.827–828) | reused from 8.538–541 | reused from 8.538–541 (+ "to every one of them" for πᾶσι μάλ’) | the published lines (iliad-051); πᾶσι μάλ’ is "all, every one" in `l` and "to every one of them" in `i`, "all alike", "quite all" |
| ἐν δὲ σὺ τοῖσι πεφήσεαι (13.829) | "and among them you will be slain" | "and you will be slain among them" | "you will be killed" (φένω "slay", πεφήσεαι "be slain"), "you will fall"; follows the Odyssey’s φένω "slay" |
| αἴ κε ταλάσσῃς μεῖναι (13.829–830) | "if you bring yourself to await" | "if you can bring yourself to await" | "if you dare" (reserved for θαρσέω), "if you endure"; follows the table’s τλάω aorist "bring oneself" (11.350) |
| ὅ τοι χρόα λειριόεντα δάψει (13.830–831) | "which your lily-like skin will tear" | "which will tear your lily-like skin" | "tender", "lily-white", "delicate"; follows λειριόεις "lily-like" (3.152) and χρώς "skin" (iliad-030), δάπτω "tear" (ἔδαψεν "tore", 5.858) |
| Τρώων κορέεις κύνας ἠδ’ οἰωνούς (13.831; Τρώων with κύνας, not partitive as in 8.379) | "the dogs and birds of the Trojans you will sate" | "you will glut the Trojans’ dogs and birds" | "you will feed Trojan dogs and birds" (loses "of the Trojans" as possessor), "one of the Trojans will sate" (the 8.379 reading, which needs τις); κορέω "sate" (`l`) / "glut" (`i`) as shipped |
| ἔμενον Τρώων ἐπιόντας ἀρίστους (13.836) | "awaited the best of the Trojans coming on" | "stood to await the best of the Trojans as they came on" | "stood firm against", "withstood" (μένω with an accusative is "await"); ἐπιόντας "coming on" |
| οὐδὲ λάθοντο ἀλκῆς (13.835–836) | "did not forget might" | "did not forget their might" | "courage", "valour", "battle-strength" ; ἀλκή "might" (θούριδος ἀλκῆς "impetuous might") |
| ἠχὴ δ’ ἀμφοτέρων ἵκετ’ αἰθέρα καὶ Διὸς αὐγάς (13.837) | "And the din of both reached the aether and the glare of Zeus" | "And the din of both sides reached the upper air and the glare of Zeus" | "the rays of Zeus" (αὐγή "rays" is kept for the sun, 8.480), "the light of Zeus", "the bright sky"; αὐγή keeps "glare" (2.456, 13.244) as the table says; αἰθήρ "aether" (`l`) / "upper air" (`i`) as at 8.555 |
